items.stem: How is a taxable temporary difference best described?

options.text: A difference between the carrying amount and the tax base that will result in taxable amounts in future periods
options.rationale: Correct: a taxable temporary difference increases future taxable profit and gives rise to a deferred tax liability.

options.text: A permanent difference that never reverses
options.rationale: Permanent differences do not create deferred tax.

options.text: A difference that only affects the current tax charge
options.rationale: Temporary differences affect deferred, not current, tax.

options.text: The difference between accounting profit and cash received
options.rationale: That is not the definition of a temporary difference.

items.explanation: Correct: a taxable temporary difference increases future taxable profit and gives rise to a deferred tax liability.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO adjustments commonly create deferred tax in consolidated financial statements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Fair-value uplifts to the acquiree's identifiable assets on a business combination
options.rationale: Correct: fair-value uplifts with no change in tax base create temporary differences.

options.text: Elimination of unrealised profit on intra-group inventory
options.rationale: Correct: eliminating unrealised intra-group profit creates a deferred tax effect.

options.text: Recording a dividend received from a third party
options.rationale: A simple dividend receipt does not of itself create a consolidation deferred tax adjustment.
Routine salary payments do not create consolidation temporary differences.

items.explanation: Correct: fair-value uplifts with no change in tax base create temporary differences.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A company revalues a building upward, recognising the gain in other comprehensive income, and the tax rate then changes. Where is the effect of the rate change on the related deferred tax recognised?

options.text: In other comprehensive income, consistent with where the original item was recognised (backwards tracing)
options.rationale: Correct: tax follows the item; the rate-change effect is recognised in OCI.

options.text: Entirely in profit or loss regardless of the original item
options.rationale: That ignores backwards tracing to OCI.
It is not a share-capital movement.

options.text: Not at all, because deferred tax is never remeasured
options.rationale: Deferred tax is remeasured for enacted rate changes.

items.explanation: Correct: tax follows the item; the rate-change effect is recognised in OCI.
